reason: Internal only, no behaviour change: no verdict moves and the gate still neither reads nor writes the decision log. The Relevance Gate's two counters now carry `conversation_id`, so a refusal can be joined to the room it refused. Before this a `no_go` said only «somewhere on Signal», and the two measures that would grade the gate against something other than its own opinion — it refused room R while she demonstrably held something for R, and a human tagged her in R within minutes of a `no_go` — were uncomputable even though both sides of the join were already in Postgres. Both series are labelled, not just the verdict one: a fail-closed no_go refuses the room exactly as a chosen one does, so a measure blind to the error series under-counts refusals by whatever the outage rate happens to be (14 of 290 over the seven days to 2026-09-16). The series stay separate — «the room was quiet» and «the gate is down» must never be one reading. Cardinality is bounded by the configured conversation roster. Also re-takes the baseline the culture-tier bundle rests on (admission 1.09% over 6.9 days, the participation turn has still run once ever, and the counters reset 19 times in 7 days so a counter cannot hold this rate at all), and re-measures the Honcho scoping claim behind DEC-182: the workspace boundary is enforced — a workspace holding nothing declines a question a workspace holding everything answers in full — so «Honcho does not scope» is narrowed to «Honcho does not scope below the workspace». No routing changed. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
